models.description: Google YAMNet â€” 521-class audio event classifier. Detects gunshot, glass break, scream, raised voices. Input: 1s of 16kHz mono audio. Output: 521-class softmax. Sali sourced/validated this for the personal-safety app's Tier 2 audio path; reused here as-is for BEACON's F6 modal-corroboration factor (docs/01 Â§4) â€” same model, new job: corroborating a camera sighting, not standing alone as a phone trigger.
models.notes: Runs in Tier 2, woken by a Tier 0 RMS amplitude gate (vision/audio_agent.py) and by the browser's DSP impact gate for Home Guard (server/src/audio/yamnet.py) -- never continuous. Input shape confirmed by direct interpreter introspection (0.975s @ 16kHz). Download source: https://tfhub.dev/google/lite-model/yamnet/classification/tflite/1. CLASSES ARE LISTED BY NAME, NOT INDEX, AND RESOLVED AT LOAD TIME against the yamnet_label_list.txt embedded in the .tflite. The previous hand-written index map was wrong -- 195/198 were recorded as glass_break but are in fact 'Bell' and 'Bicycle bell', 393/395/396 as scream but are 'Smoke detector', 'Foghorn' and 'Whistle', and 39 as raised_voices but is 'Gasp'. Resolving by name makes that class of error impossible rather than merely corrected.
